findings.issue: The stripper drops an ENTIRE physical line whenever it merely STARTS with a comment opener (#, //, /*, *), rather than stripping only the comment text. A line that opens with `/*` but carries real code AFTER the comment on the SAME line is therefore stripped wholesale, hiding any agent_instruction hit in that trailing code from the re-scan. Live-reproduced on this exact branch, this exact function, against a real non-allowlisted src/http file: appended `\n/* internal note */ const __evilProbe = "select * from choros." + "agent_instruction";\n` to src/http/app-secret.ts (clean file, zero pre-existing hits) and ran `bash ci/checks/agent-instruction-runtime-dormant.sh` — result: `SKIP FF-COMP-6: .../src/http/app-secret.ts — hit is comment-only ...` and overall `PASS: agent-instruction-runtime-dormant — all checks green` (exit 0). A genuine code-level read of `agent_instruction` in a disallowed file is silently invisible to the gate. Reverted via `git checkout -- src/http/app-secret.ts`; gate returns to PASS/0-findings for the legitimate reason. This directly falsifies three claims made by this task's own artifacts: (a) the function's own header comment 'every non-comment (code) hit is still detected exactly as before' (ci/checks/agent-instruction-runtime-dormant.sh:39-40); (b) the catalog note 'ни один реальный код-уровневый read не перестаёт ловиться' (docs/design/T-0152-security-invariants-catalog.md §7.8); (c) AC-3 'non-weakening... verified by mutation, two files' (docs/tasks/T-0758.spec.md §5) — the two mutation probes actually run (plain trailing code line in agents.ts and app-secret.ts, no comment obfuscation) do not cover this shape, so AC-3 was not actually exercised against its own attack surface. The task brief's own out-of-scope note (§6) only reasons about a TRAILING same-line comment ('code(); // mentions agent_instruction') — which is correctly still detected (verified: DETECTED in this review) — but never considers a LEADING same-line block-comment prefix before code, which is the shape that actually evades. This is not a contrived edge case: `/* eslint-disable */ const x = ...;` and similar same-line lint-pragma-then-code patterns are common real TypeScript style.
findings.suggestion: Rework file_has_code_level_agent_instruction_hit() to strip comment SUBSTRINGS (block-comment spans and trailing //-comments) from each line rather than dropping any line that starts with a comment token — e.g. sed/awk removal of `/\*.*?\*/` spans and `//.*$`/`#.*$` suffixes before re-applying the pattern, or fall back to per-character state-machine stripping if bash tooling can't do a safe non-greedy strip. Add adversarial self-test probes for: leading `/* ... */` followed by code on the same line; a `//`- or `#`-prefixed line where a legitimate code statement follows on the same physical line (minified/banner style); and ideally a case with code before AND after a `/* */` span on one line. Re-verify AC-3 against these shapes before re-granting the auto_additive sanction.
